title: Immunofluorescence staining of kidney sections to monitor ischemia-induced damage
protocol: Deparaffinize tissue sections by immersing slides in Xylene twice, each for 10 minutes.
Hydrate tissue sections by immersion in 100% ethanol for 10 minutes.
Hydrate tissue sections by immersion in 100% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Hydrate tissue sections by immersion in 95% ethanol in PBS for 5 minutes.
Hydrate tissue sections by immersion in 70% ethanol in PBS for 3 minutes.
Hydrate tissue sections by immersion in 50% ethanol in PBS for 3 minutes.
Hydrate tissue sections by immersion in 30% ethanol in PBS for 3 minutes.
Wash slides in PBS twice, each for 5 minutes.
Immerse slides in 10mM sodium citrate pH6.0/Tween-20 in a glass jar.
Microwave the jar containing the slides on high power setting for 3 minutes.
Repeat microwave treatment for an additional 3 minutes.
Allow the solution to cool down to room temperature (30-45 minutes).
Remove slide from jar and draw hydrophobic borders with a Dako-pen around each tissue section.
Add 0.1% Triton-X100 solution to permeabilize cell membranes for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Block unspecific binding sites with 5% FBS/Tween-20 solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Dilute antibodies against HuR (1:250) and aquaporin-1 (1:125) in blocking solution.
Transfer slides to a humidified chamber and add 50-100μl of primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution overnight at room temperature.
Wash with blocking solution three times, each for 5 minutes.
Dilute secondary antibodies in blocking solution (1:500 for Cy3-conjugated anti-mouse IgG; 1:250 for AlexaFluor®488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG).
Incubate slide with diluted secondary antibodies in a humid chamber for 2 hours at room temperature.
Protect the slide from light during incubation.
Wash the slide with blocking solution three times, each wash lasting 5 minutes.
Stain DNA with 1 µg/ml of stain in blocking solution for 2 minutes.
Add mounting medium to the slide.
Place a glass coverslip over the slide.
Seal the edges of the coverslip with nail polish.
Incubate one section on each slide without primary antibodies.
Proceed with adding secondary antibodies as described above.
To assess autofluorescence, process control samples without addition of primary or secondary antibodies.
